extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (U.S. patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making and drafting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103: applicable statutory grounds, required form paragraphs, determination of prior art dates (including international filing date rules), provisional rejections, and the required content and rationale in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) — Applicant Not the Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) bars the issuance of a patent where an applicant did not invent the subject matter being claimed and sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must presume the applicants are the proper inventors unless there is proof that another made the invention and that applicant derived the invention from the true inventor. See MPEP § 2137 - § 2137.02 for substantive requirements of 102(f) rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) — Prior Invention by Another
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) bars the issuance of a patent where another made the invention in the United States before applicant and had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section forms a basis for interference practice. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and MPEP § 2138 - § 2138.06 for requirements and interference procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraphs for 35 U.S.C. 102 Rejections (7.07–7.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following form paragraphs should be used in making the appropriate rejections. Note that the particular part of the reference relied upon to support the rejection should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.07 to 7.14 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action. Many form paragraphs must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 (Statement of Statutory Basis). If the statute is not being cited in an action on the merits use form paragraph 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.07 — Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for rejections under this section made in this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: The statute is no longer being re-cited in all Office actions. It is only required in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Where the statute is not being cited in an action on the merits, use form paragraph 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.08 — 102(a) Activity by Another Before Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) the invention was known or used by others in this country, or patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country, before the invention thereof by the applicant for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.09 — 102(b) Activity More Than One Year Prior to Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) the invention was patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country or in public use or on sale in this country, more than one year prior to the date of application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by paragraph form 7.07, and may be preceded by form paragraph 7.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.10 — 102(c) Invention Abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) he has abandoned the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09. See MPEP § 2134 for establishing abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.11 — 102(d) Foreign Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) the invention was first patented or caused to be patented... in a foreign country prior to the date of the application for patent in this country... filed more than twelve months before the filing of the application in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08 to 7.10. See MPEP § 2135 for applicable 102(d) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.12 — 102(e) Patent/Application Publication to Another with Earlier Filing Date (AIPA & 2002 Amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) the invention was described in (1) an application for patent, published under section 122(b), by another filed in the United States before the invention by the applicant... or (2) a patent granted on an application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention by the applicant for patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should only be used if the reference is (a) filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a); or (b) a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from, or a U.S. or WIPO publication of, an international application if the international application has an international filing date on or after November 29, 2000. In determining the 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals (119(e)), nonprovisionals (120/121), and internationals (120/121/365(c)) only if the subject matter used is appropriately supported in the relied upon earlier-filed application's disclosure. Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)-(d) and 365(a). Detailed examiner notes (1–8) explain international filing date, language, designation, and pre-/post-AIPA considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.12.01 — Pre-AIPA 102(e) (Refs from International Applications Filed Prior to Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) the invention was described in a patent granted on an application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention... (pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph when the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from a national stage of, or a continuing application claiming benefit under 365(c) to, an international application having an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000. Examiner notes explain determination of the reference's 102(e) date and caution that WIPO publication may give earlier prior art date under 102(a) or (b). Consider benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals/nonprovisionals and internationals only if supported in the earlier disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.13 — 102(f) Applicant Not the Inventor (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) he did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08 to 7.12. See MPEP § 2137 for supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.14 — 102(g) Priority of Invention (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) during the course of an interference... another inventor ... establishes... that before such person's invention thereof the invention was made by such other inventor and not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed, or (2) before such person's invention thereof, the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08 to 7.13. In determining priority consider dates of conception and reduction to practice and reasonable diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.15 and Variants — Generic 102 Rejection Language and Follow-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.15 Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a), (b) Patent or Publication, and (g): 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102[2] as being [3] by [4].' (Instructions for bracket insertions provided.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and form paragraphs 7.08, 7.09, and 7.14 as appropriate, or by form paragraph 7.103, and must be followed by either form paragraph 7.15.02 or 7.15.03. Use bracket instructions to indicate anticipation vs. clear anticipation and to identify prior art relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.15.01 — Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (Common Assignee or Common Inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to provisionally reject over an earlier-filed copending application that discloses the claimed invention and has either a common assignee or at least one common inventor. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date, it would constitute prior art under 102(e) if published or patented. This provisional rejection might be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 (derivation), 37 CFR 1.131 (date of invention), or other appropriate actions. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.15.02 — 102(e) Rejection (Common Assignee or Inventor(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 102(e). The rejection might be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed was derived from the inventor of this application or by a showing under 37 CFR 1.131. Apply AIPA and 2002 amendments to determine 102(e) dates when appropriate; use pre-AIPA 7.12.01 when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.15.03 — 102(e) Rejection (No Common Assignee or Inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reject over a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date that discloses but does not claim the same invention; the patent or publication is not required to have a common assignee or inventor. Apply AIPA/2002 rules or pre-AIPA 7.12.01 as appropriate when determining the reference's 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.16 — 102(b) Public Use or On Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.09 or by form paragraph 7.103. A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.17 — 102(c) Abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by paragraphs 7.07 and 7.10 or by paragraph 7.103. Insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment. See MPEP § 2134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.18 — 102(d) Foreign Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants' [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.11 or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 3 insert an explanation including appropriate dates and how they make the foreign patent available under 35 U.S.C. 102(d). See MPEP § 2135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.19 — 102(f) Applicant Not the Inventor (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded either by paragraphs 7.07 and 7.13 or by paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2 insert an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP § 2137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents Required in a 35 U.S.C. 103 (Obviousness) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: After indicating that the rejection is under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner should set forth in the Office action: (A) the relevant teachings of the prior art relied upon; (B) the difference(s) in the claim over the applied reference(s); (C) the proposed modification of the applied reference(s) necessary to arrive at the claimed subject matter; and (D) an explanation as to why the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support an obviousness conclusion, either the references must expressly or impliedly suggest the claimed invention or the examiner must present a convincing line of reasoning as to why the artisan would have found the claimed invention to have been obvious in light of the references (Ex parte Clapp). Preferably cite relevant column/page/line numbers. See MPEP § 2141 - § 2144.09 and § 2145 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Every Reference Relied Upon in the Rejection Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference is relied on to support a rejection, whether or not in a minor capacity, that reference should be positively included in the statement of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Hoch. Inclusion helps the applicant identify issues and is important for later interpretation of patent scope if the application issues as a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of Written Record and Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important for an examiner to properly communicate the basis for a rejection so that the issues can be identified early and the applicant can be given fair opportunity to reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written record must clearly explain the rationale for decisions made during prosecution because examiners normally cannot be compelled to testify regarding their mental processes. Clear explanation aids applicants and future legal proceedings (35 U.S.C. 282/261 implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection Using Provisional Prior Art Under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional 103 rejections should be made in later-filed copending applications when earlier-filed copending applications (not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)) have different filing dates and would be prior art under 102(e), unless excluded under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejections alert applicants they can expect an actual rejection if the earlier application issues; they preserve confidentiality of unpublished applications. Provisional rejections apply when copending applications have a common assignee or a common inventor. They can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability over the earlier application; (B) combining subject matter into a single application claiming 120 benefit; (C) filing a 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit showing derivation; (D) filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing an earlier date of invention; or (E) showing common ownership or CREATE Act 103(c) disqualification for applications pending on/after Dec 10, 2004.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103(c) / CREATE Act Disqualification — Commonly Assigned or Joint Research Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter which was prior art under former 103 via 102(e) may be disqualified as prior art if it was, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person. The CREATE Act further provides joint research agreement disqualification if three conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three CREATE Act conditions: (A) the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made; (B) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (C) the application for patent discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement. These rules affect whether provisional 103 rejections should be made and apply to patents granted on or after Dec 10, 2004 (with transitional rules for earlier grants/applications). See MPEP § 706.02(l)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Double Patenting and Terminal Disclaimer Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims of copending applications conflict, a provisional double patenting rejection should also be given; where the applications claim the same patentable invention, a terminal disclaimer and a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit may be used to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 in a common ownership situation if the earlier application has been published or matured into a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining copending applications into a single application may avoid a provisional rejection; however, combining into a continuation-in-part has implications for 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit and entitlement. See MPEP § 718 and examples provided.
